issues.title: Traditional namespace declaration with braces
issues.description: The rule requires C# files to use file-scoped namespace declarations (ending with semicolon without braces), but this file uses traditional namespace declarations with opening and closing braces.

issues.title: Incorrect type conversion in generic component parameter assertion
issues.description: The test validates a generic component with an int type parameter but uses Convert.ToInt64 instead of Convert.ToInt32 to assert the parameter value. Since the parameter is defined as int (System.Int32) in GenericTestComponent<int>, this creates a type mismatch. The assertion compares a long (Int64) value to the expected int (Int32) value 42, which will cause the test to fail even though the component deserialization is working correctly. This breaks the validation logic for generic component parameters.

issues.title: Incorrect sequence validation for multiple generic components
issues.description: The test validates deserialization of multiple closed generic components but checks that both descriptors have sequence number 0 instead of verifying that the second descriptor has sequence number 1. Component descriptors in a collection must have sequential ordering starting from 0, and this test should verify the second component has sequence 1. This incorrect assertion fails to validate proper sequence ordering, which is critical for component initialization and rendering order in Blazor.

issues.title: Generic type parameter mismatch in component marker validation
issues.description: The test creates and renders a GenericComponent<int> with value 456, but then validates the component marker against GenericComponent<string> type instead of GenericComponent<int>. This causes the test to check for the wrong fully qualified type name and assembly metadata. The type validation will fail because the actual rendered component is GenericComponent<int> while the test expects GenericComponent<string>, breaking the validation of WebAssembly component prerendering for closed generic types.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #64643 - Add test coverage for prerendering closed generic components

structured_output.summary:
This PR is test-only. It adds a `GenericComponent<TValue>` Razor test component and new tests that check closed generic components (`GenericComponent<int>`, `GenericComponent<string>`) can be rendered statically, prerendered in Interactive Server mode, and prerendered in Interactive WebAssembly mode. It also adds `ServerComponentDeserializerTest` cases that round-trip closed generic type names and parameters through the server marker serializer and deserializer. The coverage is worthwhile: the server-mode tests check the protected descriptor contents (assembly name, assembly-qualified type name, parameter definitions and values), not just that rendering succeeded.

Two problems need fixing before merge. First, the WebAssembly ClientMode test renders `GenericComponent<int>` but asserts the preamble's `TypeName` against `GenericComponent<string>.FullName`, so the test will fail as written. Second, the deserializer test file's namespace was changed from file-scoped to block-scoped and the class body was not re-indented. That adds unrelated churn and breaks the file's formatting.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The WebAssembly ClientMode test asserts the wrong type name (`GenericComponent<string>` against a render of `GenericComponent<int>`), so it fails deterministically. Fixing that is required. The namespace and indentation churn is a smaller maintainability issue that should be cleaned up in the same revision.

architecture.overview:
Prerendering a root component goes through `EndpointHtmlRenderer.PrerenderComponentAsync`, which writes a `ComponentMarker` (defined in src/Shared/Components/ComponentMarker.cs). For Interactive Server, `ServerComponentSerializer` protects the type name and parameters into the marker descriptor, and `ServerComponentDeserializer` reverses that on the circuit side. For Interactive WebAssembly, `WebAssemblyComponentSerializer` writes the assembly name and the full type name directly into the marker in plain form. Before this PR, closed generic component types were never exercised through these paths by tests. The PR adds no production code. It adds tests and one test component that use the existing serialization paths, so the behavior is locked in.

The new tests assert on the marker and descriptor contents (assembly name, `Type.FullName`, parameter definitions), not only on whether rendering succeeded. That makes them useful as regression tests for the type-name round-trip. The WebAssembly test has an assertion that targets the wrong closed type, which is the main correctness issue in this change.
steps: Start at the render entry point: the tests call `renderer.PrerenderComponentAsync` with `typeof(GenericComponent<T>)` and a render mode (null/static, `InteractiveServerRenderMode`, or `RenderMode.InteractiveWebAssembly`).

For Interactive Server, the marker descriptor is produced by `ServerComponentSerializer` and protected with the data protection purpose. The new server-mode tests unprotect it and assert `AssemblyName`, `TypeName` (`Type.FullName` of the closed generic), `ParameterDefinitions`, and `ParameterValues`.

On the circuit side, `ServerComponentDeserializer.TryDeserializeComponentDescriptorCollection` rebuilds the `ComponentType`. The new deserializer tests check that closed generic types with `int` and `string` arguments come back as the same `FullName`, and that parameter values survive the round trip.

For WebAssembly, `WebAssemblyComponentSerializer` writes the rendered type's assembly and full type name into the marker. The ClientMode test checks those values, but it is currently checking `GenericComponent<string>` while rendering `GenericComponent<int>`.

The new `GenericComponent.razor` in `TestComponents` provides the single generic component used across both test files. Its `Value` parameter is typed as `TValue`, so the parameter definition carries the closed argument type.

findings.title: WebAssembly ClientMode test asserts the wrong closed generic type
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/Endpoints/test/EndpointHtmlRendererTest.cs`, the test `CanPrerender_ClosedGenericComponent_ClientMode` (around lines 817-838) renders `typeof(GenericComponent<int>)` but its preamble assertions at lines 837-838 compare against `typeof(GenericComponent<string>)`. Change both assertions to use `GenericComponent<int>` so they match the rendered type. Keep the existing assertion shape and do not change the render itself. Then confirm the test's `TypeName` expectation matches what `WebAssemblyComponentSerializer` writes into the marker.

findings.title: Unrelated namespace and indentation rewrite in deserializer test file
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/Server/test/Circuits/ServerComponentDeserializerTest.cs`, the namespace was changed from file-scoped (`namespace Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Server.Circuits;`) to block-scoped, and the class body was not re-indented. Restore the original file-scoped namespace declaration and the original class declaration at the top of the file, with the body at its original indentation. Remove the extra closing brace added at the end of the file. Keep the new `using System.Globalization;` and the new tests and `GenericTestComponent<T>` helper unchanged, so the diff shows only the added code.

findings.title: Server-mode closed generic test verifies the protected descriptor contents
findings.body: `CanRender_ClosedGenericComponent_ServerMode` and `CanPrerender_ClosedGenericComponent_ServerMode` go past a simple render check. They unprotect the descriptor and assert `AssemblyName`, `TypeName` against `typeof(GenericComponent<T>).FullName`, the parameter definition's name and assembly-qualified `TypeName`, and the parameter value. Asserting on the serialized type name is the part of the feature the original issue cares about, so these tests would catch a regression in the type-name round trip. This is a good pattern to keep for the WebAssembly path once its assertion is corrected.

findings.title: Deserializer tests cover the closed generic round trip with multiple type arguments
findings.body: The new deserializer tests cover a closed generic with an `int` argument, one with a `string` argument, a parameterized case, and a case with two closed generic markers in one batch. The helper `GenericTestComponent<T>` follows the same style as the existing `TestComponent` and `DynamicallyAddedComponent` helpers, so the test file stays consistent in its helper design.
